shortTheory.question: Why is Chemistry divided into many branches?
shortTheory.answer: To understand the widely spread complex subject of chemistry and to concentrate on its specific aspects, chemistry is divided into many distinct branches. These branches have distinct areas of study for the scientists to focus on and to achieve breakthroughs and advancements.

shortTheory.question: Which branches of Chemistry study reactions involving electrons outside the nucleus and reactions inside the nucleus?
shortTheory.answer: Physical chemistry investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels. Nuclear chemistry deals with the reactions taking place in the nucleus of an atom.

shortTheory.question: In which state does matter exist in the Sun?
Which form of matter do most material things in this world belong to?
shortTheory.answer: Mixtures. Air, soil, milk and tap water are everyday examples of mixtures.

shortTheory.question: Where is the difference between organic chemistry and biochemistry?
shortTheory.answer: Organic chemistry deals with carbon compounds, while biochemistry is the study of chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms.

shortTheory.question: Which branch of Chemistry studies chemical and biochemical phenomena in the environment?
shortTheory.answer: Environmental chemistry is the scientific study of the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in this planet.

definitions.text: Chemistry is the branch of science which deals with the properties, composition and the structure of substances. It also deals with the physical and chemical changes in matter and the laws or principles which govern these changes.

This branch investigates how substances behave at atomic and molecular levels. It provides clear explanation as to how fundamental physical laws governing our world cause atoms and molecules to show specific characteristics and in turn react to give huge structures related to life. Physical chemistry is also used to predict and change the rates of reactions and thus optimize the conditions to carry out the reactions on industrial scale.
It is the study of the synthesis, composition, properties and structure of elements and compounds that contain little or no carbon.
It is the branch of chemistry that deals with the carbon compounds (hydrocarbons and their derivatives) other than its simple salts like carbonates, bicarbonates, oxides and carbides.
It is the scientific study of the chemical and biochemical phenomena that occur in this planet.
This branch of chemistry deals with the analysis of different substances. It involves separation, identification and determination of the concentration of the components present in material things.
It is the branch of chemistry in which we understand life through chemical processes. It is the study of chemical substances and vital processes occurring in living organisms.
Nuclear chemistry deals with the reactions taking place in the nucleus of an atom. It deals with radioactivity, nuclear processes and transformation in the nuclei of atoms.
Anything other than energy which carries weight and occupies volume is called matter.
A state of matter is one of the many distinct forms in which matter can exist.
Plasma can be considered as a partially ionized gas containing electrons, ions, photons, etc.
The solubility of a solute is the amount of solute which can dissolve in 100g of a solvent at a particular temperature.

fullMarks: For a question asking you to name a branch, write the branch first, then give a brief reason linked to the topic: reaction rate—physical chemistry; digestion—biochemistry; ecosystem—environmental chemistry; wavelength absorption measurement—analytical chemistry.
For organic versus inorganic chemistry, compare the kinds of compounds studied: carbon compounds in organic chemistry and elements or compounds containing little or no carbon in inorganic chemistry.
For organic chemistry versus biochemistry, make the distinction clear: organic chemistry focuses on carbon compounds; biochemistry focuses on chemical substances and processes in living organisms.
For a plasma answer, state that it is a partially ionized gas and include examples or particles from the text, such as electrons, ions and photons, where relevant.

For a crystallization answer, describe the steps in order: dissolve potassium nitrate in hot water, cool the solution so crystals form, separate the crystals, and dry them. Link the process to the increased solubility of solids in hot water.
When describing solubility, include the amount, the solvent and the temperature: it is the amount of solute that dissolves in 100 g of solvent at a particular temperature.

mistakes: Mixing up physical chemistry and nuclear chemistry. Fix: nuclear chemistry studies reactions in the nucleus; physical chemistry studies the behaviour of substances at atomic and molecular levels.
Calling biochemistry simply the study of all carbon compounds. Fix: say that it studies chemical substances and vital processes in living organisms.
Confusing plasma with an ordinary gas. Fix: describe plasma as a partially ionized gas containing particles such as electrons and ions.

Answering that most material things are elements or compounds when the question asks for the form most material things belong to. Fix: answer mixtures and give examples such as air, soil, milk or tap water.

Mixing up environmental and analytical chemistry. Fix: environmental chemistry studies chemical phenomena in the environment; analytical chemistry separates, identifies and determines components in substances.
Describing crystallization without explaining why crystals form. Fix: mention that a solid such as potassium nitrate is more soluble in hot water and crystals form as the solution cools.
